correctness.rationale: Scott continuity on the positive-diagram subspace preserves specialization order, hence diagram inclusions map to subset inclusions. If A0 subset B0 subset A1 are positive diagrams of endpoint-isomorphic but middle-nonisomorphic structures, a reduction to E0 forces endpoint output symmetric difference finite; the nested middle output must then differ from either endpoint by only a finite set, contradiction. For each E_n, choose countably infinite infinite target equivalence classes, reserve one subcollection as full infinite classes in B_m and take m-element subsets of another to form finite m-classes; repeat inside B_m to obtain A_n with finite n-classes. Induced substructures preserve equality/inequality facts, and domains can be nested proper subsets of N as in the cited positive-text learning definition. The proof is infinite and order-theoretic; no finite experiment is offered as a substitute.
residual_risks: The theorem would not apply to a learning domain artificially restricted to distinct copies all on the same full underlying domain N; the actual cited text-learning framework permits domains subset of N.

originality.rationale: The standard Cantor-continuous full-diagram E0 criterion and the known positive-data TxtEx-completeness are credited. Bazhenov et al. (2024) Proposition 6 already uses Scott monotonicity for an embedding obstruction, so the monotonicity *technique* is not new. The separately scoped statement is an order-convexity obstruction for the specific target E0 and its application to a canonical TxtEx-complete equivalence-structure family; it rules out the naive direct E0 analogue raised in their Question 1 but does not solve that entire characterization. Priority of an equivalent generic monotonicity lemma is a residual risk.
